en.title: Minimum Cost to Make All Sizes Distinct by Increasing
en.description:
Each product's size can only increase, and each unit of increase costs that product's cost. In the end all product sizes must be distinct; find the minimum total cost. Products cannot be removed.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n, the second line the sizes, and the third line the unit costs. 1≤n≤200000, 1≤size≤10^9, 1≤cost≤10000.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 6, 7 and 1. In the second example the 3 with cost 4 rises to 4 and the 2 with cost 1 rises to 5, total 7.
hints: Sort by original size and scan the final size coordinates, keeping in a max-heap the products whose original size is ≤ the current position; at each position, fix the one with the highest unit cost. When no product is available, jump straight to the next original size.
